It serves one concern and uses the shared CustomBaseEntity abstraction consistently. However, the rule that `description` must be unique is declared twice. It is stated once as a class-level constraint, @Unique(['description']), and again as a property-level index, @Index({ unique: true }) on `description`. The rubric requires each rule or invariant to live in one place, so this duplication fails it. In TypeORM, these two declarations typically create two separate unique constraints or indexes for the same column, and the two declarations can drift apart over time. The rest of the entity is cohesive.
